result: {"findings": [{"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 381, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "isClosed() cannot tell a real close from a spurious win; it reports true while operations are still in flight", "body": "The doc comment tells a select driver to use `isClosed()` to separate a real close (\"stop draining\") from the spurious `error.Closed` that `getResult` documents at line 302-321. The negative direction is sound: `closed` is monotonic, so `isClosed() == false` does prove the win was spurious. The positive direction, which is the one that makes the driver stop, is not sound. `getResult` returns `error.Closed` whenever `completed` is empty, and a real drained state needs `closed and pending.isEmpty()` (see `isReady` at line 325 and `wait` at line 185). `close` explicitly leaves in-flight operations running (line 148-149). So the sequence is: another task calls `close()` over in-flight operations, a stale futex wake wins the queue arm, `getResult` pops nothing and returns `error.Closed`, and `isClosed()` now answers true. The driver reads that as a real close and tears down while operations are still pending. Those completions are never handed out, so for the heap-backed operations that the module header requires for cross-task submission (line 16-20) the driver drops the only pointers to them: a leak, and a loop callback that later writes into memory the driver considers finished. There is a second, smaller race in the same direction: even a genuinely spurious win can be followed by a `close()` from another task before the driver calls `isClosed()`, which flips the answer under the driver. The predicate the contract needs is the drained state itself, taken under one lock, not `closed` alone: expose `isDrained()` returning `self.closed and self.pending.isEmpty()` (the same expression `isReady` already uses), or state in this doc comment that the driver must also check `hasPending()` and re-poll while it is true."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 386, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "New public isClosed() has no test", "body": "Every other public query on this type (`isEmpty`, `hasPending`, `hasCompleted`) is exercised by the tests in this file, and the close semantics have dedicated tests at lines 575, 941, 986 and 1087. `isClosed` adds a public observation with a documented discriminator contract and no test asserts any of it: not false on a fresh queue, not true after `close()`, and above all not the state it reports after a canceled `wait` closes the queue through `closeAndKeepResults` (line 556) or while operations are still pending after a close. Without a test, the value the contract rests on is unpinned, and a later change to when `closed` is set breaks the documented discriminator silently."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 386, "severity": "trivial", "category": "style", "title": "isClosed() is placed inside the future-protocol block", "body": "The comment at line 278-288 opens the \"Future protocol implementation\" section, and `isClosed` is inserted between `asyncWait` and `asyncCancelWait`, which are the two halves of that protocol. `isClosed` is a general state query and belongs with `isEmpty`, `hasPending` and `hasCompleted` at lines 244-263.
